prompt: Re-carve this photo as a close-up of a white marble head sculpted in the manner of Praxiteles' Hermes (c. 340 BC) and the head of Michelangelo's David, the classical ideal of ancient Greek sculpture, photographed in a museum. Every face becomes smooth, polished white marble with a soft translucent glow and faint grey veining, its exact features and expression carved in the stone. Eyes are sculpted with deeply incised irises and pupils, so the gaze stays alive and intense. Hair and beard become deep, crisply undercut curls that follow their real hairstyle and length. Any visible neck, shoulders and clothing are carved in the same marble, with clothing as simple draped cloth. Glasses, hijabs and hats are carved in the same marble. Soft museum spotlight from above-left against a plain charcoal background.
